title: Ruby's Birdy House
markdown:
The sun sparkled on the garden path. It made everything look bright and happy. Ruby loved this time of day. She especially loved watching the birds fly in and out of the big oak tree.

“Look, Dash,” she whispered to her floppy-eared dog. Dash wiggled with excitement. “See that little robin’s nest? It’s like a perfect little bowl on that branch.” Dash wagged, big brown eyes following where she pointed.

A big gust of wind rushed through the garden. The leaves danced. The oak swayed. Ruby’s heart did a little flutter, then settled. The nest wobbled. With a soft plop, it landed on the soft green grass.

Three tiny baby birds tumbled out. They landed softly and blinked. Ruby hurried over, Dash trotting beside her. She gently touched the nest. A few twigs had come loose. It was a bit wobbly. Not a disaster. A job.

“We need to build them a new, safe home.” She looked at the other nests in the tree. “But how do birds build their nests so strong?”

Mr Clive, the kind gardener, walked over. A warm smile. “That’s a clever question, Ruby. Let’s watch the birds very carefully.”

So Ruby, Dash, and Mr Clive stood very still and watched. A busy robin flew by with a beak full of sticky mud. Dab, dab, dab. The robin smoothed the mud between some twigs. Then a little sparrow wove thin blades of grass into a soft round shape.

Ruby’s eyes sparkled. “I see it. They use the sticky mud to hold the twigs together. And they weave the grass to make the inside cozy.”

She looked at the fallen nest. “The outside is like a bumpy circle, and the inside is a smooth circle. A cup. That’s a strong shape. And the round opening is easy to hop into.” Dash sniffed the nest and gave a happy woof.

“You’ve got it, Ruby.” Mr Clive smiled. “Birds are wonderful builders. Strong shapes. The best things to build with.”

Then the building began. Mr Clive found sturdy thin twigs. Ruby collected soft dry grass from under the rose bushes. Dash sniffed out wonderfully sticky mud near the pond. Ruby showed them how to shape the twigs into a round cup. They used the sticky mud to stick the twigs together, making the walls hold. Then they wove the soft grass inside for a cozy bed.

“Now, a good spot.” Mr Clive pointed to a strong low branch. “Safe here.” Together they gently placed their brand-new nest onto the branch.

The mama robin flew over. She looked at the new nest, chirped, and hopped inside. She nudged her babies closer. They snuggled in, chirping.

Ruby giggled. “We copied the birds. Sticky mud, soft grass, a strong round cup. It worked.” Dash’s tail thumped a happy rhythm on the grass.

Mr Clive nodded. “Nature has many clever ideas if you look closely.” Ruby smiled, eyes already looking around the garden, curious about what other secrets were waiting.
characters: Ruby (a shape spotter), Dash (a dog), Clive (a gardener)
author: StoryGen Community
